newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Telkom privatisation seen helping rand.
newsitem.headline: S.African Telkom privatisation seen helping rand.

text.p: The rand should benefit from the inflow of proceeds from the sale 30 percent of state telecommunications concern Telkom, although the extent to which it would strengthen was unclear, forex dealers said on Tuesday.
Deputy president Thabo Mbeki announced that $1 billion of the proceeds of the sale to a consortium comprising SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd would be injected back into Telkom.
The total value of the Telkom stake is estimated by analysts at around $1.3 billion and Mbeki said the balance of the proceeds would go to the state.

Foreign exchange traders said that while the news was positive for sentiment, its impact on the rand/dollar exchange rate was difficult to guage as it was unclear how the money would be brought into the country.

"I think for sentiment it is positive," said a senior trader who asked not to be named. "Exchange rate wise it should strengthen the rand but to what extent I don't know because I don't know how it is going to come in," she said.
First National Bank chief forex trade Dave Sadler said: "It depends on whether the Reserve Bank allows them to put (the proceeds) into the market or not."

Telkom chairman Dikgang Moseneke said that sale of the stake would be settled by a one-off payment in dollars, which would be paid at the close of the deal which could be one week to 90 days from the signing, now expected within the next few days.

"It may be done as a straight deal with the Reserve Bank and therefore the market wouldn't see it. If they put the whole thing through the market then obviously the rand will strengthen, but I doubt the Reserve Bank will allow that volume to come directly into the market," Sadler said.
Traders said that the rand should have reacted positively to the news, but that it was being hampered by month-end importer demand.
"The rand hasn't reacted much...it should have reacted positively, but we're seeing a bit of demand from importers and on back of that market might be slightly on the short side," a trader said.
The rand was last trading at 4.4200/4230 against the dollar from 4.4240/4270 overnight.
